question.leadin: Answer these questions about American women's history.
question.text: This constitutional amendment, first proposed in 1923, would ban sex-based discrimination. Although Virginia became the thirty-eighth state to ratify this amendment in January 2020, it has not yet been added to the constitution.
question.clue: This legislation failed to pass since only 35 ratified it by 1979.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about famous campaign ads.
swap.text: The "Daisy" ad was aired in 1964 by this successor of John F. Kennedy. It depicted a girl counting petals on a daisy, followed by the explosion of a nuclear weapon.
swap.answerHtml: Lyndon Baines Johnson [or LBJ; prompt on Johnson alone; do NOT accept or prompt on "Andrew Johnson"]
swap.clue: This President championed the Great Society, and the Civil Rights Act of 1964 was passed during his tenure.

question.leadin: This man declared "segregation now, segregation tomorrow, segregation forever," then tried to back that up by standing in the door to block two black students from entering his state's university in Tuscaloosa.
question.text: Name this politician. His wife, Lurleen, ran for governor when he was term-limited in 1966.
question.clue: During this man's 1972 presidential run with former Air Force general Curtis LeMay, he was shot and paralyzed by Arthur Bremer.

swap.text: This man's campaign used the slogan "In your guts, you know he's nuts" to mock Goldwater's slogan. This president defeated Goldwater in 1964 after succeeding Kennedy.
swap.clue: In the Senate, he perfected a strategy of intimidation that involved standing uncomfortably close known as "The Treatment."

question.leadin: Answer the following about African-American history referenced in Angie Thomas's novel The Hate U Give.
question.text: In the Carters' house, a photo of this man wielding a rifle and peering out of his window hangs beside a painting of Black Jesus. The Black Panther reading list contains this civil rights activist's autobiography, which was finished by Alex Haley after his 1965 assassination.
question.clue: This man's autobiography, which was adapted by Spike Lee, includes an account of his 1964 hajj and his "second conversion" to Sunni.

swap.leadin: In 1984, this politician became the second African-American after Shirley Chisholm to run for President.
swap.text: Name this civil rights activist. In his 1984 campaign, this politician assembled a progressive Rainbow Coalition to challenge for the Democratic nomination.
swap.clue: This man's failed 1988 campaign for president aimed to mobilize a "Rainbow Coalition" of minorities and progressives.

question.text: Dewey's running mate in the election was this Governor of California. This man was later appointed Chief Justice by Dwight Eisenhower.
question.clue: The John Birch Society funded billboards calling to impeach this man from a position in which he asserted that "legislators represent people, not trees or acres."

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about US health care reform in the 20th century.
swap.text: This series of domestic reforms introduced Medicare and Medicaid.
swap.answerHtml: Great Society [prompt on descriptive answers such as Lyndon Baines Johnson's social reforms]
swap.clue: Largely overseen by Bill Moyers and Richard Goodwin, it also saw the creation of the National Endowment for the Arts, and was originally outlined during a commencement speech at the University of Michigan.

question.leadin: Decided along with California v. Stewart, it held that "the atmosphere and environment of incommunicado interrogation as it exists today is inherently intimidating, and works to undermine the privilege against self-incrimination."
question.text: Name this 1966 Supreme Court decision that mandated that police inform suspects of the rights to remain silent and consult an attorney.
question.clue: In a famous partial dissent, Justice Tom C. Clark claimed that the majority opinion in this case went "too far too fast."

swap.leadin: A 1944 Act of Parliament concerning these institutions is popularly named for R. A. Butler and enshrined the Tripartite System.
swap.text: Identify these British institutions, subject to the A-Level system. The Clarendon Commission reformed how the one named Harrow was governed.
swap.clue: Social unrest prompted the 1968 division, into French- and Dutch-speaking sites, of one of these institutions in Leuven.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Vietnam War protests.
swap.text: Under the leadership of Stokely Carmichael, this civil rights organization broadened its purview to include opposing the Vietnam War. It organized sit-ins and freedom rides, and was especially popular at universities.
swap.answerHtml: SNCC [pronounced “snick”; or Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee or Student National Coordinating Committee]
swap.clue: This civil-rights organization once led by Stokely Carmichael. This organization was founded by students, and it led the Freedom Rides.

question.leadin: Workers in this industry striked under the slogan "I AM a Man."
question.text: Name this industry, whose workers began striking in response to the deaths of Echol Cole and Robert Walker. Martin Luther King Jr. was in Memphis supporting the strike in this industry in 1968 when he was assassinated.
question.answerHtml: sanitation industry [or garbagemen; or any other answers suggesting garbage collection; or Memphis sanitation strike]
question.clue: This industry's use of "wiener barrel" trucks declined after Echol Cole and Robert Walker's deaths triggered a strike that popularized the slogan "I AM A MAN."

swap.text: In this decade, patrons of a Milwaukee gay bar defended attacks from homophobic sailors in the Black Nite Uprising, presaging ("PRESS-idge-ing") "riots" at the end of this decade around an establishment owned by the Genovese crime family.
swap.answerHtml: 1960s [prompt on 60s] (The Stonewall riots took place in 1969.)
swap.clue: Tommie Smith and John Carlos raise their fists on an Olympic podium in a photo from this decade.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the life of famous Yippie Jerry Rubin.
question.text: Rubin rose to prominence in the Berkeley Free Speech Movement along with this activst, who implored young Americans to "put your bodies upon the gears" in 1964.
question.clue: The volunteers at Freedom Summer included this Italian who led the Free Speech Movement at UC-Berkeley, and famously exhorted people to "put your bodies upon the gears" during a sit-in speech in 1964.

swap.text: Rabbis Abraham Heschel and Maurice Davis were photographed walking arm-in-arm with King during the 1965 marches from this Alabama city to Montgomery.
swap.clue: While not delivered here, the "How Long, Not Long" speech describes this city as a "shining moment in the conscience of man."After seeing the televised violence here, Lyndon Johnson gave a speech which ended with "And we shall overcome."

question.leadin: This group cited the writings of Michelle Wallace to argue that, if they had freedom, it would necessitate the destruction of oppression, as opposed to starting from below.
question.text: Name this lesbian socialist collective whose members included Demita Frazier and Margo Okazawa-Rey. It took its name from an action taken by the 2nd South Carolina Infantry in June 1863.

swap.leadin: This field secretary for the NAACP was assassinated in his driveway in 1963, and his assassin Byron De La Beckwith was finally convicted in 1994.
swap.text: Name this D-Day veteran, who tried to integrate his state's public law school in 1954.

question.leadin: Section 2 of this act was the subject of the case Bartlett v. Strickland, while a 2009 Supreme Court ruling provided more leeway for statesto subvert its pivotal Section 5, but declined to rule on that section's constitutionality. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this legislation, whose major requirement for specifically identified areas to gain "preclearance" from the Justice Department remains enforced. It was also the subject of the "King Letter" over its sections involving multilingualism.
question.clue: Among the provisions of this legislation was a triggering clause that required federal pre-clearance of procedural changes.

swap.leadin: Critics of this legislation asked why more Catholic school students didn't become nuns.
swap.text: Name this eponymous initiative placed on the California ballot in 1978, which would have declared teachers who engaged in "public homosexual activity" to be "unfit for service."
